guizhou-heritage-sites-demolition.whole: All 18 participating villages submitted conservation goals to planning authorities and 26,900 people were given access to improved sanitation, both targets met, and the project renovated 1,040 traditional houses against 1,225 planned at appraisal and a target cut to 823 at the 2014 restructuring. It trained 3,215 people in traditional and tourism-related skills, with 290 trained in intangible heritage against a target of 250, improved 69 kilometres of access roads and paths, and improved the facilities at three natural heritage sites. Annual tourist visits to the key project sites reached 4.08 million at loan closing against a target of 4.36 million that was never changed, and the completion report records 4.49 million by 15 September 2017, three months after closing, attributing the shortfall at closing in part to heavier than normal seasonal rain in 2016 at the Shanmu River Scenic Park, which is known for rafting. Visitors to the gateway town information centres at Jianhe, Leishan and Liping came to 4,800 against a revised target of 4,500 and an appraisal target of 8,500, the fourth centre in Guiyang having been dropped during restructuring. Two more works were dropped at the July 2014 restructuring: the museum for the Dingxiao National Geo-Park, for want of a feasible design, and the Provincial Tourist Information and Service Centre, for want of suitable land, which the Independent Evaluation Group's review says reduced project costs by about US$2.36 million. Average income at project sites rose from RMB 3,160 a person in 2010 to RMB 6,131 in 2016, employment in tourism and hospitality at those sites from 3,023 people in 2010 to 13,551 in 2016, and in five project areas the number of people counted as poor fell from 18,181 in 2010, when the poverty line was RMB 650 a person a year, to 14,735 in 2016, when it was RMB 3,160. The report says the project's own share in these changes cannot be established: it produced no tracer studies of the people it trained, did not track the residence or ethnicity of those who gained from tourism, and records tourist numbers across Guizhou growing 24 per cent a year from 2011 to 2015. Economic rates of return recalculated for four sample sites at completion were 17.8 per cent at Wanfenglin and 19.1 per cent at Jiuzhou, both above their appraisal figures, and 17.5 per cent at Langde and 12.4 per cent at Zhaoxing, both below; the appraisal figures are 13.7, 10.2, 19.6 and 12.6 per cent in the report's table, while the report's own text and the review summarise them as a range from 13.7 to 19.6 per cent, labelling 13.7 as Jiuzhou. Both the report and the review rate efficiency Substantial. Final cost was US$94.85 million including interest during construction, about 105.6 per cent of the US$89.84 million estimated at appraisal. All these figures are the lender's own, from its completion report and the Evaluation Group's review of it; no independent check was found.

kunming-line-3-jinmasi-relocation.whole: The project built Line 3's 38.2 kilometres of track and all 17 of its stations, both targets met, and the line opened in August 2017. Average weekday ridership after six months of operation was 153,800, against 200,000 at appraisal and a target cut to 150,000 at the 2015 restructuring. Peak-period travel time between two origin and destination pairs on the corridor fell from 43 minutes to 14 and from 38 minutes to 15, against targets of 22.5 and 17.5; on-time performance was 99 per cent against a target of 98, user satisfaction 91.2 per cent against 80, and the floor area ratio of new development along the line 1.6 times the surrounding district's against a target above 1. Thirteen of the 17 stations had bus or bicycle facilities within 50 metres of an exit, which the completion report puts at 76 per cent of its target, and four of the 17 interchange works were delayed, with their road construction and pavements unfinished at closing. The restructuring of bus routes to feed the metro was recorded as only partly achieved: an integrated fare card was in use and 12 new feeder routes were introduced, but the report says it may take three years before all the feeder routes run, which it counts as cutting the rate of return by 0.2 percentage points. Six indicators were dropped at the March 2015 restructuring, among them the ridership and revenue attributable to Line 3, the rail company's working ratio, and the share of new development occurring along rail lines. The transit-oriented development proposed in 2013 and 2014 above the Shizui depot was cancelled in 2015 and the design reverted to the depot as approved, and station and depot developments at the eastern end of the line were cancelled or postponed as the property market worsened. The report puts the economic rate of return at 7.9 per cent over a 30-year period, covering 99 per cent of project cost, against an appraisal figure its own table gives as 8.5 per cent and the Evaluation Group's review reads from the appraisal document as 8.0 per cent. The report's paragraph 44 gives relevance High and efficacy and efficiency Substantial; the review rates efficiency Substantial, noting the project was 19 months late partly because Kunming delayed the start of construction while three metro lines were being built at once and partly because of household relocation, and adding that complex metro projects can now be supported at much lower rates of return than at appraisal because benefits such as access to jobs and land values are counted. Spending came to US$1,803.9 million against US$1,711.6 million estimated at appraisal, with the US$300 million loan revised to US$276.9 million and that amount disbursed. All these figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.
kunming-line-3-jinmasi-relocation.why: ICR00004604 (P117656_ICR): Annex 1 results framework for 38.2 km track, 17 stations, ridership 153,800 against original 200,000 and revised 150,000, on-time 99 against 98, travel times 43 to 14 against 22.5 and 38 to 15 against 17.5 (both count minutes of journey time, so lower is better), user satisfaction 91.2 against 80, FAR 1.6 against >1, stations with bus/bicycle facilities 13 of 17 (76 per cent), bus-route restructuring 'partially yes'. hunan-gansu-small-towns-demolition.whole: By the completion report's count the project built 91.96 kilometres of road against 136.94 planned at appraisal and a target cut to 119 at the December 2015 restructuring, 43.08 kilometres of that in Gansu against a revised 83.20, and rehabilitated 20.37 kilometres against 20.94 at appraisal and a revised 18.60. It gave 134,279 people piped water against 79,665 at appraisal and a revised 89,000 and made 20,123 new household connections against 9,120 and a revised 12,300; 554,080 people were counted as benefiting from the new and rehabilitated roads, against 540,400 at appraisal and a revised 640,000, and in Hunan that figure was 37,386 against 13,900 at appraisal and a revised 150,000. Hunan is where the zeros sit: no one was recorded as gaining access to water or solid waste management services against 15,900 at appraisal and a revised 10,500, no users of the integrated centres, markets and irrigation facilities against 11,341 and a revised 15,000, no market sales revenue and no market vendors against revised targets of RMB 55 million and 430 vendors, and no farmer organisations against five at appraisal and a revised target of zero. One town that was to build a farmers' market was dropped from the project and the results framework was not updated to match. Across the three provinces 17 new markets, industrial centres and vocational training centres were built against 23 at appraisal and a revised 18, irrigation was improved on 4,874 hectares against 5,690 and a revised 5,840, 1,226 market vendors were recorded against 3,265 and a revised 2,954, 52,076 people were trained against 40,421 and a revised 62,000, 35 studies were completed against 22 and a revised 26, and 1,789 project office staff were trained against 1,352 and a revised 1,340. The wastewater treatment plant built in Hunan reached its design capacity of 3,000 cubic metres a day, but the report records it running at a third of that capacity with unit treatment costs rising, kept going by subsidies from higher-level government with no wastewater fee collected, and says the markets built in Yueshan and Dingziwan had not drawn enough vendors by closing. Of the 28 towns at appraisal, four were dropped at the 2015 restructuring - Fuxing and Dongli in Guangdong, Zhentou in Hunan and Wenfeng in Gansu - with Xiantang added, leaving 25. The national programme for small towns that the project was to be designed and carried out with was cancelled during preparation, which the report says partly explains the shortage of counterpart funding; the project was downgraded to problem status in June 2014 and never left it. The report gives economic rates of return recalculated at completion of 9 to 16 per cent for roads in Hunan, where none was calculated at appraisal, 12.1 per cent for roads in Gansu against 10 to 15 per cent at appraisal, 26 per cent for irrigation in Gansu against 14 to 22 per cent, and 14.4 per cent for Gansu's agricultural markets, for which no appraisal figure existed; both the report and the Evaluation Group's review rate efficiency Substantial and the outcome Moderately Unsatisfactory, the review rating relevance of objectives Substantial where the report rates it High. Total cost fell from US$296.64 million at appraisal to US$213.18 million, and US$1,571,787.65 of the three loans, about 1 per cent, was cancelled at closing. The beneficiary satisfaction figure of 82 per cent against a 75 per cent target comes from a social and economic impact survey agreed as a remedial measure under the project; every other figure here is the lender's own, and no independent check was found.

wushan-hospital-landslide-resettlement.whole: By the completion report's count six hospitals were built, renovated or equipped against eight at appraisal and a target cut to six at the June 2020 restructuring, and all eight project hospitals got a standardised cost accounting system producing quarterly departmental unit costs, telemedicine for tele-diagnosis and a place in an annual performance assessment report. The share of inpatients referred up to higher-level hospitals fell from 8.5 per cent to 4.4, against a target tightened from 6 to 5 per cent at the 2017 restructuring, and the average length of stay fell from 10.6 days to 7.5 against a target tightened from 8.5 to 8 days. Twenty high-volume conditions were treated using clinical pathways against 10 at appraisal and a revised 16; 98 community and township health centres signed referral agreements against 5 at appraisal and a revised 42; 1,863 health staff were trained against a target of 1,400 that was set only at the 2017 restructuring; 637 trainees finished courses with a certificate against 600; and six evaluations of pre-reform packages were done against three at appraisal and a revised one. Outpatient visits at the eight hospitals rose from 1.62 million in 2012 to 2.80 million in 2019 and inpatient admissions from 120,600 to 201,600, figures the report calls additional indicators outside the results framework, and patient satisfaction was 92.85 per cent against a 90 per cent target, on an indicator added in 2020 and measured only in 2019 and 2020. The scope was cut as Wushan's and Qianjiang's hospitals left the loan: Qianjiang county withdrew after securing domestic finance and returned US$13.97 million, Wushan county returned US$4.71 million after the landslide stopped its hospital, US$10 million was cancelled at the October 2019 restructuring and US$8.68 million was moved to three other hospitals. The report says the Bank had put about US$5 million into the Wushan traditional Chinese medicine hospital by the time of the landslide and that this investment has had no return so far and may not have any return in the future. No economic or financial rate of return was calculated at appraisal or at completion; the report's partial analysis puts the net benefit at about RMB 314 million (US$48 million) against a project cost of about RMB 555 million, and both the report and the Evaluation Group's review rate efficiency Modest, on 41 months of extension, 8.5 years from Board approval to closing, and a disbursement rate under 10 per cent in the first four years and 27 per cent near the end of the fifth. Spending came to US$140.8 million against US$155.5 million estimated at appraisal. All these figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.

xuancheng-industry-zone-house-demolition.whole: The project built 52 kilometres of non-rural road with storm-water drains, water supply and sewers against 65 planned at appraisal and a target cut to 50 at the 2018 restructuring, and a wastewater treatment plant with its collection network. By the completion report's count net employment in the zone reached 6,449 jobs against 32,000 at appraisal and a revised target of 5,700, incremental value added RMB 1,090 million against 2,300 million at appraisal and a revised 990 million, and 215 firms were attracted against 220 at appraisal and a revised 200; women were 26 per cent of the new jobs against 18 per cent at appraisal and a revised 25 per cent. 18,813 people were given improved water sources and improved sanitation against 80,000 at appraisal and a revised 18,000; the plant treated 9,000 cubic metres a day to Class 1A standard against 17,500 at appraisal and a revised 3,000; and wastewater treatment covered the whole project area against an 80 per cent target set in 2018. One row fell short on its own terms: 35.6 tonnes a year of biochemical oxygen demand were removed against 1,213 tonnes at appraisal and a revised 153 tonnes, which the report attributes to less sewage reaching the plant than expected and to the zone administration's own environmental standards for the firms in the park, leaving the collected wastewater much less polluted than assumed. An intelligent investment promotion system, a labour market information system, an internal monitoring system covering more than 300 companies and a real-time environmental monitoring system were all delivered. The project area was cut from 20.2 to 14.6 square kilometres at the January 2017 restructuring, cancelling ten roads with their underground networks and one overpass, and the loan was cut at the same time from US$150 million to US$90 million, with the disbursement share for civil works raised from 61 to 100 per cent; five more roads were cancelled later, and 1,984.15 mu of land was acquired against 2,558.1 mu in the resettlement plan. The report puts the economic rate of return at completion at 6.8 per cent counting employment and wages and 14.7 per cent counting total value added, against 10.4 and 32.7 per cent at appraisal, and attributes the fall to the longer development period and less commercial development than expected; both the report and the Evaluation Group's review rate efficiency Substantial, the review's table giving 32.7 per cent at appraisal and 14.7 per cent at completion over 97.9 and 97.1 per cent of project cost. The report also records savings of US$4.6 million in mid-2018 spent on extra water quality monitoring equipment, 22 contracts of which only a few overran, and tenders often drawing 30 to 40 bids. Spending came to US$168.9 million against US$343.6 million estimated at appraisal, with US$87.3 million of the loan disbursed. The satisfaction figure of 74.2 per cent against a 70 per cent target comes from a survey run four times under the project, whose overall satisfaction fell from 74 to 72 per cent between the third and fourth rounds; every other figure here is the lender's own, and no independent check was found.

moba-gorge-forest-land-compensation.whole: By the completion report's count the project rehabilitated 218 kilometres of non-rural road in Sichuan against a target of 200 and 36.1 kilometres in Gansu against 35.9, restored traffic to pre-earthquake levels on all project roads, and supported 14 water utilities in Sichuan - six wastewater plants and eight water treatment plants, with 116.5 kilometres of water supply pipe, 442.9 kilometres of sewage and drainage pipe and four booster pumping stations - and five in Gansu, with three wastewater plants, two water plants, 62.8 kilometres of water supply pipe and 109.2 kilometres of sewers. It built, renovated or equipped 60 health facilities in Sichuan and seven in Gansu and 186 classrooms in Gansu; beds in Sichuan's project facilities rose from 3,221 before the earthquake to 5,374, and the report puts the population served by the health works at 9.82 million. Six of those rows, the road, utility, health facility and classroom counts, are Bank-wide core indicators added in June 2014 with no appraisal target. One row fell short: half of Gansu's county towns were recorded as having water supply restored at least to pre-earthquake levels against a target of all of them, because the Cheng county water treatment plant had not been completed or connected and was expected to operate in June 2017, once the Moba Gorge reservoir had been filled. Primary schools were dropped from the project and paid for under China's own earthquake recovery programme, and the Evaluation Group's review records that resettlement problems delayed roads in Wuhu district and Cheng county and that some roads were dropped or realigned to reduce the resettlement needed. The Moba Gorge dam and its water plant were 23 months late, cost about US$31 million between them, and are put by the review at 32 per cent of the cost of the infrastructure part of the recovery programme; in Sichuan, loan savings of about US$41 million together with extra counterpart funds paid for a third batch of works, all of which were finished except one small road. No economic analysis was done at appraisal, because the loan was an emergency operation, and none was done at completion: the report assessed cost effectiveness, service restoration and local economic recovery instead, and says the savings to local governments from more resilient infrastructure after the 2013 Lushan earthquake could not be quantified. The completion report rates efficiency Substantial and the outcome Satisfactory; the Evaluation Group's review rates efficiency Modest, capacity building in Gansu Modest and the outcome Moderately Satisfactory. Of the US$710 million loan, US$695.80 million was disbursed. All these figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.

zhamushui-guangrun-resettlement-postpone.whole: The Guangrun component's two stations have a combined installed capacity of 28.4 MW, and the carbon finance completion report records generation at about half what was expected. Against an appraisal figure of 95.66 GWh a year, output was 11.44 GWh in 2010, 11.77 in 2011, 11.80 in 2012, 26.51 in 2013, 46.27 in 2014, 36.22 in 2015, 46.39 in 2016, 53.00 in 2017 - its best year, at 55 per cent of the design figure - 33.00 in 2018 and 16 in 2019. Certified emission reductions contracted under the purchase agreement were cut from 485,000 to 249,590 and then to 157,745 because generation fell, and 145,699 were delivered, the last monitoring period yielding 94,924 against 104,970 contracted. The component overran its 2006 appraisal estimate by 90 per cent, a cost overrun of US$32.86 million, which the report attributes to unexpected geological conditions, higher prices for labour and raw materials, higher interest during construction and the cost of resettlement, most of it incurred after the Bank loan closed in 2011. Construction was still unfinished in December 2019: a decision on the right bank slope treatment and the crest spillway sluice gates at Zhamushui had not been taken, and two water diversion tunnels and the second-stage treatment of the Hongwawu reservoir's right bank were suspended pending two water allocation disputes with a neighbouring province. All of the county town's drinking water comes from the Zhamushui reservoir at an agreed charge of 0.41 yuan a cubic metre, about 12 million yuan a year, which the report's footnote says the county government never paid; the project company stopped paying the Bank loan and interest in 2013, about 8 million yuan a year, and the county government paid instead, more than 30 million yuan by early 2019. An advance payment of US$388,000 against the carbon credits funded a community benefit plan in the nine villages affected, finished in early 2011 with an acceptance report in May 2011, and 20 per cent of the component's value added tax went to the Jianshi county poverty alleviation fund for the six years 2012 to 2017; the report puts the rise in income of the people directly affected at about 18.37 per cent against 2007, and lists among the project's benefits improved flood control and water supply for more than 70,000 people in Jianshi county and more than 1,500 construction jobs with 60 permanent posts. The financial rate of return on total investment was 5.44 per cent at appraisal without carbon revenue and 7 per cent with it, against a benchmark of 8 per cent, and at completion is below zero, about minus 3.12 per cent, with income half the appraisal figure and investment twice it. The economic rate of return for Guangrun at the 2020 report is minus 0.6 per cent excluding emission benefits, 0.0 per cent with local emission benefits and 2.7 per cent with local and global benefits, against 2.7, 4.2 and 9.1 per cent for the same component in 2012 and 9.5, 11.0 and 16.0 per cent for the five-component project as a whole. The report rates the loan project's relevance High, efficacy Modest, efficiency Negligible and outcome Unsatisfactory, and the carbon finance operation's efficacy Substantial; it records that the owner, Guodian, has classified the project as a negative asset and was negotiating to sell it back to the Jianshi county government. All these figures are the lender's own, from the Bank's completion report on the carbon finance operation and the Evaluation Group's assessment of the parent project; no independent check was found.
zhamushui-guangrun-resettlement-postpone.why: Report 153668 (P094795_ICR), the carbon finance ICR: data sheet section F Table 1 for the three monitoring periods (10,391; 42,384; 94,924 against 104,970) and the 157,745/145,699 totals; ratings summary section C for outcomes U; paragraphs 7 and 15-18 for 28.4 MW, the ownership change, the two closing extensions, the US$32.86 million overrun at 90 per cent above the 2006 estimate with its four named causes, the unfinished works at both stations as of December 2019 and the two water disputes, and the CER volume cut from 485,000 to 249,590 to 157,745; paragraphs 19-20 for relevance High and the benefit list including 70,000 people, 1,500 construction jobs and 60 permanent posts; paragraphs 23-26 and Table 1 for the year-by-year generation against 95.66 GWh and efficacy Modest; paragraph 25 and footnote 6 for the water charge of 0.41 yuan per m3, about 12 million yuan a year, never paid, the company stopping loan payments in 2013 and the county paying more than RMB 30 million by early 2019; paragraphs 27-31 for the US$388,000 advance, the nine villages, the completion of the community benefit plan in early 2011, the 20 per cent of VAT for 2012-2017, the 18.37 per cent income rise and efficacy Substantial for the carbon operation; paragraphs 32-37 and Tables 2 and 3 for the FIRR (5.44 and 7 per cent at appraisal against a benchmark of 8; below zero at ICR, about -3.12 per cent in footnote 7), the EIRR rows for Guangrun in 2012 and 2020 and for the entire project, the US$13 million spent 2012-2017 on geological problems, efficiency Negligible, and Guodian's classification of the project as a negative asset and the sale negotiations. The PPAR (127227) is the Evaluation Group's assessment of the parent project and is the source the ICR cites for the unchanged tariff; no figure is taken from it here. Note on independence: the Evaluation Group sits inside the World Bank Group, so its assessment is not an independent check.

wuhan-middle-ring-resettlement-overrun.whole: The Evaluation Group's review reports that the project carried out 41 schemes - 26 road segments, four interchanges and 11 pedestrian facilities - and added an 8.2 kilometre connection from the Sanjintan interchange to the fourth Yangtze rail bridge, which could not be provided for at appraisal because the bridge's location had not been settled. Travel time was measured at three locations: at the first the target was met exactly, a five-minute improvement on the baseline; at the second the saving was one minute better than target; at the third the result was three minutes short of target but three minutes better than the baseline, which the review attributes to continuing peak-hour congestion on a bridge over the Han river. Average daily bus ridership rose from 2.59 million person trips in 2002 to 4.54 million against a target of 3.10 million, while Wuhan's travel demand grew 70 per cent between 2002 and 2009 and the public transport share of trips stayed at about 23 to 24 per cent. The vehicle emission control strategy and a new vehicle inspection facility were completed as planned; the road maintenance management system was installed three years late and its data were still being collected at closing, so it could not yet produce the annual maintenance plans intended at appraisal. The third sub-objective, reform of bus service delivery, is rated Negligible: the technical assistance study was completed to the Bank's satisfaction, but Wuhan decided to keep public transport within government rather than tender bus routes competitively, which was the indicator for that sub-objective. Works were dropped along the way: four roads and two interchanges, as not yet needed at the traffic volumes seen; eight of eleven passenger interchanges and five of twelve terminals, over low user volumes, land acquisition problems and timing; a pedestrianised street, because no agreement could be reached on the site; and three bus priority lanes, because of construction works on the routes. Eight safety enhancement corridors were added, some blackspot sites having already been treated with local funds. Project cost net of the front-end fee rose by US$713 million, the first of the five reasons the review lists being a US$321 million increase in the cost of resettlement, and the borrower's contribution rose 279 per cent from US$398.20 million to US$1,110.66 million. The review puts the economic rate of return at 21.4 per cent at completion against 23 per cent at appraisal, at a 12 per cent discount rate and covering 94 and 93 per cent of project cost, and rates efficiency Substantial. It rates the outcome Moderately Satisfactory against the completion report's Satisfactory and Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory against the report's Satisfactory, and records that the Bank's Quality Assurance Group rated quality at entry satisfactory in seven of the nine areas it assessed and moderately satisfactory in two, one of them the resettlement process. On road safety the review reports that deaths in Wuchang district, mostly pedestrians and cyclists, were halved over the project, while printing the figures as 23 in 2004 and 65 in 2009, which its own sentence contradicts. Every figure here comes through the Evaluation Group's review of the completion report; all are the lender's own, and no independent check was found.
wuhan-middle-ring-resettlement-overrun.why: ICRR13574 (P069852_ICRR) is the only evaluative document for this project in the cache; it was read in full. Section 2c for the 41 schemes, the 8.2 km Sanjintan connection and the dropped works (four roads and two interchanges; eight of eleven interchanges; five of twelve terminals; the pedestrianised street; three bus priority lanes; eight safety corridors added). Section 2d for the US$713 million cost rise with the US$321 million resettlement increase first in the list, the borrower contribution rising 279 per cent from US$398.20m to US$1,110.66m, US$199m of the US$200m loan disbursed, and the one-year extension. Section 4 for the three travel-time measurements, the Wuchang fatality sentence (reported as printed, with its internal contradiction stated rather than resolved), the RMMS three-year delay, bus ridership 2.59m to 4.54m against 3.10m, the 70 per cent growth in travel demand and the 23-24 per cent modal share, and the Negligible rating on bus reform with competitive route tendering as the indicator. Section 5 and its rate table for ERR 23 per cent at appraisal over 93 per cent of cost and 21.4 per cent at the ICR over 94 per cent, a 12 per cent discount rate and efficiency Substantial. Absence claim: no completion report for P069852 is in the cache, so no figure is claimed from the ICR directly; the paragraph says so. The 2004 PAD was not used for delivery figures.

tedap-ukonga-mzinga-wayleaves.whole: By the completion report's count the project built or rehabilitated 184.4 kilometres of distribution line against a target of 282 kilometres set at the 2015 restructuring, and 37.1 kilometres of transmission line against 57.1: 13 kilometres of the Ubungo to Kurasini section could not be built because the national roads agency's Mandela Road expansion took the wayleave, and the 1.3 kilometres at Mzinga Creek was still being procured and installed at closing, with completion expected on 31 March 2018. The report says the 132 kV southern ring circuit planned for Dar es Salaam, running from the Factory Zone III substation through Factory Zone II, Mbagala and Kurasini to Ubungo, was removed from the project's scope for that reason, so the ring circuit could not be realised in the time available. End-user voltage reached 220 volts against a target of 218 from a baseline of 190; losses in the project area fell from 28 per cent to 16.44 against a target of 21; collection efficiency rose from 70 per cent to 94 against a target of 95; 25.45 MW of grid-connected small power generation was installed against 17 MW at appraisal and a revised 25 MW; 85,000 prepaid meters were installed against a target of 60,000; and 30,933 people were connected under the on-grid component against a revised target of 25,000. On the off-grid side the rural energy agency concluded 65 subproject transactions against a revised target of 10, standard power purchase agreements covered 58.3 MW of installed capacity against a revised 20 MW, rural household connections reached 71,966 against a target of 40,000, 144,622 households were connected under that component against a revised target of 110,000, which the report converts to 694,189 people at 4.8 people a household, and 206,149 direct beneficiaries were recorded against 20,000 at appraisal and a revised 114,000. Two rows fell short: customer satisfaction at the utility was 62 per cent against a target of 75, a gap the report calls 13 percentage points, and community connections - dispensaries, health centres, secondary schools, staff houses, police posts and public lighting - came to 996 against a revised 1,200. Activities cancelled: the customer management system with its trouble and resource management modules, and the centralised call centre and high-value customer cell, both over budget overruns, with the first later taken into another Bank project; and in 2009 the procurement of four distribution packages after the Bank objected to the bidding. The report puts the project's economic rate of return at 13 per cent with a net present value of TZS 24 billion (US$19 million) at a 10 per cent discount rate, covering 99 per cent of project cost, with the grid component at 17 per cent against 31 per cent at appraisal and one of the two mini-grids analysed returning a negative rate; no rate of return for the project as a whole was given at appraisal. Both the report and the Evaluation Group's review rate efficiency Modest and the outcome Moderately Satisfactory on a split rating. Spending came to US$143.67 million against US$171.88 million at appraisal, with no borrower contribution, and the project closed five and a half years after its original date. All these figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.
tedap-ukonga-mzinga-wayleaves.why: ICR00004395 (P101645_ICR): Annex 1 results framework for end-user voltage 220 against 218, hydropower 25.45 MW against 17 original and 25 revised, customer satisfaction 62 against 75, collection 94 against 95, losses 16.44 against 21, rural connections 71,966 against 40,000, direct beneficiaries 206,149 against 20,000 and 114,000, on-grid household connections 30,933 against 25,000, REA transactions 65 against 10, prepaid meters 85,000 against 60,000, distribution lines 184.408 km against a revised 282 (the row's original-target column is 0.00 because the target was set at the 2015 restructuring), transmission lines 37.1 km against 57.1 with the comment naming the 13 km Ubungo-Kurasini portion lost to the TANROADS road expansion and the 1.3 km at Mzinga Creek with the 31 March 2018 date, SPPA capacity 58.3 MW against 20, community connections 996 against 1,200, and household connections under component B 144,622 against 110,000 with the 694,189 people at 4.8 per household. ctb-kwabenya-stone-crackers.whole: In Ghana the project built the 330 kV Aboadze to Tema transmission line with its terminal substations, which the completion report says were commissioned in late 2009; upgraded switchgear and electromechanical equipment at the Aboadze switchyard and the Volta switching system, including circuit breakers, disconnect switches and protection and control facilities; installed telecommunication equipment for the third bulk supply point at the Accra East and Achimota substations; and upgraded the supervisory control and data acquisition and energy management systems, with the Akosombo and Kpong generating station reinforcements and the control centre completed by June 2013. A dam safety assessment and an emergency preparedness plan for the Akosombo, Kpong and Nangbeto stations were delivered, and power sector monitoring data for the regional member states were collected and disseminated. In Benin and Togo the new dispatching centre at the bi-national utility's headquarters and the backup centre in Cotonou were completed and operating at closing, and the dispatch modernisation, rehabilitation and emergency plan studies and a draft procedures manual were finished. Every outcome indicator was recorded at its baseline value or at nil, because the regional project was not commissioned by the closing date: no electricity was traded over the project's infrastructure, power losses along the interconnection links stayed at 6, 4, 8 and 4 per cent for the four utilities against a 2 per cent target for each, and the targets for outage reduction, detection and response time, delivered capacity and reactive power are all recorded as not achieved. Construction along the 330 kV line in Benin was unfinished when the Bank closed the financing of that activity on 30 June 2016, the report saying the Bank no longer had the resources for it, and the cooperation agreement for the backbone is recorded as not in place. The Volta River Authority's control centre study was not completed and its training centre was not set up. At appraisal the Evaluation Group's review gives economic rates of return of 16 per cent for Ghana and 35 per cent for Benin on components accounting for 85 and 87 per cent of the appraisal estimates, with a net present value of US$64 million at a 10 per cent discount rate. At completion only the Ghana investments could be analysed: with the line loaded at about 15 per cent of its 400 MW nominal capacity the benefit-cost ratio is below 1 and the rate of return below 12 per cent, and the report says 12 per cent needs the load factor at about 70 per cent together with a wider cost difference between the western and eastern areas, and a better result needs the remaining investments and more natural gas. Gas through the West African Gas Pipeline did not materialise, so there was limited production to send over the line at its design capacity. Both the report and the review rate efficiency Negligible and the outcome Unsatisfactory, and the report puts the risk to the development outcome High. All these figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.
ctb-kwabenya-stone-crackers.why: ICR00004338 (P075994_ICR): section F results framework read row by row - three PDO indicators and nine intermediate indicators - each recorded at baseline or nil with the comment that the transmission project had not been commissioned by the completion date, except the emergency preparedness plans (deployed 20 December 2013) and the power sector M&E data (completed 14 April 2016), with the cooperation agreement 'Not in place'. Absence claim: no recalculated project-wide rate exists - the ICR says the project cannot reasonably be evaluated as a regional project because it was not completed; both documents' efficiency sections were read in full.

wapp-apl3-zagtouli-bolgatanga-deaths.whole: The project built the 225 kV line from Bolgatanga in Ghana to the Zagtouli substation at Ouagadougou - about 210 kilometres, of which 171 ran from Zagtouli to the border and 17 from the border to Bolgatanga - a new 330/225/161 kV substation at Bolgatanga, an extension of the 225/90 kV Zagtouli substation and a new 90/33 kV substation in Burkina Faso, telecommunications, supervisory control and energy management systems, and the 330/161 kV transformer at Aboadze; it also funded strengthened management of the Kabore Tambi National Park and the feasibility and environmental studies for a further line. Every indicator was met or exceeded by the completion report's count: the weighted average annual cost of electricity supply in Burkina Faso fell from US$0.26 to US$0.20 a kilowatt-hour against a target of US$0.25; the annual duration of outages from generation shortfall and load shedding fell from 130 hours to 8, its target; the interconnection line ran 8,497 hours in the year against a target of 7,884; exports from Ghana to Burkina Faso reached 222 GWh against a target of 158; 3,474 rural households along the right of way were connected against a target of 3,400; 20,844 people were counted as direct beneficiaries against 20,400, 55 per cent of them women, the target; and 82 staff were trained in live network operation and maintenance against 81. The Evaluation Group's 2022 assessment of the project reports outages down to 33 minutes a year and exports up to 1,777 GWh in 2022, a figure its own overview prints as 1,177 GWh, with imports from Ghana then about 48 per cent of Burkina Faso's electricity supply, and says sustaining the lower cost is uncertain because it turns on surplus power in Ghana, oil prices, fuel transport costs, demand growth and the security situation. The report puts the economic rate of return at 29.7 per cent at completion against 32.6 per cent at appraisal, with a net present value of US$230 million at a 10 per cent discount rate against US$284 million, over 95 per cent of project cost, and the financial return at 29.6 per cent for Burkina Faso's utility against 37 per cent at appraisal and 13.47 per cent for Ghana's against 12.2 per cent; incremental transmission losses were 2.3 per cent against 5 per cent assumed at appraisal, and 1.13 per cent measured in 2018, when the line had run half a year. Both the report and the Evaluation Group's review rate efficiency Substantial and the outcome Satisfactory, and both rate overall Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory. The project took 18 months from approval to effectiveness because of cross-conditions among the three financiers, and the Bank withdrew its money from the line itself and put it into the Bolgatanga substation, with the French Development Agency moving the other way, to get past disagreements over joint procurement. The completion report's financing table records nothing at completion from the French Development Agency, the European Investment Bank or the two borrowers, against US$32.3 million, US$30.9 million and US$5.9 million planned at approval, and a total actual cost of US$36.3 million against US$111 million at approval. All these figures are the lender's own, from its completion report and the Evaluation Group's review and later assessment of it; no independent check was found.
wapp-apl3-zagtouli-bolgatanga-deaths.why: ICR00004695 (P094919_ICR): Annex 1 results framework for all three PDO and six intermediate rows - cost of supply 0.26 to 0.20 against 0.25, outages 130 to 8, hours of operation 8,497 against 7,884, exports 222 GWh against 158, households in the right of way 3,474 against 3,400, direct beneficiaries 20,844 against 20,400 with 55 per cent women, staff trained 82 against 81, Kintampo-Tamale studies and the Aboadze transformer both Yes - and the key outputs table for the 210 km of line, the Bolgatanga substation, the Zagtouli extension, the new 90/33 kV substation, the SCADA/EMS and the Kabore Tambi park work. benin-iame-transmission-compensation.whole: The project built 284.7 kilometres of 161 kV transmission line against a target of 310 - the 30 kilometre Sakete to Tanzoun line and the 254.7 kilometre Onigbolo to Parakou line, whose length fell from an estimated 280 kilometres when the design and right of way were finalised - and the completion report records the Onigbolo to Parakou line completed in November 2018 and the transmission network meeting the N-1 reliability criterion, its target. It rehabilitated and reinforced the distribution networks of Cotonou, Porto-Novo, Sakete, Bohicon, Allada, Parakou and Natitingou, after which measurement campaigns found voltage fluctuation above 7 per cent eliminated in those cities; installed 45,000 prepayment meters and 350,000 compact fluorescent bulbs, both targets; developed and applied efficiency standards for bulbs and air conditioners; brought 300,000 hectares of the Moyen Oueme protected area under forest management plans with rural wood markets installed; and trained 1,150 people in improved carbonisation and logging techniques against a target of 450. People with electricity through household connections reached 3,880,116 against a target of 3,900,000, which the report calls almost achieved, on 210,735 new subscribers between 2009 and 2017 plus 7,168 connections in the first quarter of 2018; direct beneficiaries were put at 2,214,235 against a target of 200,000. Three rows fell short. Losses on Benin's transmission network were 67.6 GWh at completion against a target of 24 GWh and a baseline of 51 GWh; the report gives the same figures as a loss rate falling from 5.44 per cent in 2009 to 4.8 per cent in 2018 on a flow that grew from 937 to 1,409 GWh, and attributes the 2017 rise to poor supply voltage from Nigeria and to the Bohicon to Onigbolo line being out of service while the Sakete to Onigbolo line was built. Losses in the project area were 23.09 per cent against a target of 20 and a baseline of 22, the non-technical part 13.09 per cent against 10, which the report says the project was not designed to address. And the energy efficiency component's savings came to 6.61 MW of peak load and 12.06 GWh against targets of 9.7 MW and 14 GWh, because 40-watt bulbs were replaced as well as the 60-watt bulbs assumed. None of the four planned stand-alone rural generation systems was built: after the rural electrification concession study was delayed, the money was moved at the 2013 restructuring to on-grid electrification of new localities. The report's recalculated economic rates of return are 36 per cent for the transmission lines against 22 per cent at appraisal, 40 per cent for distribution against 16 per cent, and 92 per cent for energy efficiency against 53 per cent, at a 10 per cent discount rate, and it notes the transmission figures use the appraisal assumptions because the line was finished just before closing and no data on its effect existed; the Evaluation Group's review records an appraisal rate of 20 per cent covering 55 per cent of project cost and no recalculated rate in its own table. Both the report and the review rate efficiency Modest and the outcome Moderately Satisfactory, on a project that closed three and a half years after its original date. The appraisal's financial projections for the two utilities proved highly inaccurate, the report says, both companies' finances having worsened significantly since 2010 with public-sector non-payment and persistent losses, and no financial analysis was done at completion. The credit was cut to US$54.38 million and US$52.78 million was disbursed. All these figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.

pakistan-edtip-crop-compensation.whole: The completion report records 65 per cent of the planned subprojects completed and 73 per cent of the Bank financing disbursed. Of the subprojects planned, 11 of 13 were completed at the Hyderabad distribution company, 25 of 31 at Islamabad, 8 of 31 at Lahore and 31 of 39 at Multan, with grid stations at Bahter More, Gangal, Saggian, Mominpura and D G Khan unfinished at closing and expected during 2014. In the transmission component the new 220 kV grid station at Kassowal was about 79 per cent complete, some 20 months past its scheduled date and expected in December 2014, with about US$6 million of the cost falling beyond closing on the national transmission company; its transmission line was complete. Because Kassowal was unfinished, loading at the Yousufwala and Vehari grid stations stayed at 100 per cent against targets of 77 and 74 per cent. Losses fell at two companies and rose at two: Islamabad's annual transmission and distribution losses came to 8.6 per cent from a baseline of 12.2, beating both the appraisal target of 11.4 and the revised 9.55; Multan's 17.6 per cent beat a revised 18.0 but not the appraisal 17.4, and stayed above the regulator's 15 per cent for that year; Hyderabad's 33.2 per cent was worse than a revised target of 32.2 and far above the regulator's 24.9 per cent; and Lahore's 13.2 per cent was worse than its own 12.8 baseline and worse than a target revised upwards to 12.1. Electricity handled met revised targets at Islamabad, 8,830 GWh against 8,784 after a cut from 11,640, and at Multan, 13,274 against 12,830 after a cut from 14,398, and missed them at Hyderabad, 9,356 against 9,683, and Lahore, 16,458 against 18,126, which the report attributes to the country's supply shortfall. Collection as a share of billing fell short at three companies - Islamabad 90.0 per cent against a revised 95.9, Hyderabad 67.6 against a revised 73.5, Multan 93.2 against 99.5 - the report noting non-payment by public-sector consumers, collection from private consumers close to 100 per cent, and that this indicator is not related to the project's works. Training targets were met on a cumulative basis, with 936 staff trained at Islamabad, 320 at Hyderabad, 667 at Lahore and 855 at Multan between 2007 and 2013. Dropped at the June 2012 restructuring: distribution works worth about US$38.28 million held not to be urgently needed, technical assistance worth about US$8.72 million, and the whole energy efficiency component, about US$15 million; US$62 million of the loan, a quarter of it, was cancelled then and about US$2 million more in February 2014. A further US$32 million of contracts were never awarded, among them two new grid stations in Lahore and 40 MVA power transformers that the Lahore company's board later scrapped, and a distribution transformer contract in Multan stopped by a High Court stay order; contracts worth about US$56 million were not completed by the closing date. The report puts the economic rate of return at 47 per cent at completion against 22 per cent at appraisal, covering 97 and 90 per cent of project cost, with the loss reduction works returning most of the gain because power purchase costs had more than tripled since appraisal; it rates efficiency Substantial, as does the Evaluation Group's review, and both rate the overall outcome Moderately Unsatisfactory, the report saying the project missed 50 per cent of its targets. All these figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.
pakistan-edtip-crop-compensation.why: ICR3137 (P095982_ICR): section F results framework read row by row for all 18 PDO indicators and the intermediate rows used - Yousufwala and Vehari loading 100 against 77 and 74 with Kassowal named as the cause in both comments; IESCO electricity handled 8,830 against a revised 8,784 (original 11,640), losses 8.6 against 11.4 and 9.55, collection 90.0 against a revised 95.9, training 272 in year with 936 cumulative; HESCO 9,356 against 9,683, losses 33.2 against 32.2 with the NEPRA 24.9 per cent figure, collection 67.6 against 73.5, training 320 cumulative; LESCO 16,458 against 18,126, losses 13.2 against a target revised upwards to 12.1, collection 97.9 against 97.5, training 667 cumulative; MEPCO 13,274 against 12,830, losses 17.6 against 18.0 revised and 17.4 original with the NEPRA 15 per cent figure, collection 93.2 against 99.5, training 855 cumulative. Table 2.2 for the subproject counts by company and the five unfinished grid stations; the Component B section for Kassowal at about 79 per cent, 20 months late, December 2014 and the US$6 million beyond closing; the Component A/C sections and paragraph 1.6 for the dropped works (US$38.28m, US$8.72m, US$15m) and paragraph 1.3 and Annex 1 note for the US$62 million cancellation in June 2012 and US$2 million in February 2014; the paragraph at p.2330 of the text file for the four high-value contracts not awarded (Askari X, Punjab University, 40 MVA transformers, the MEPCO 200 kVA contract under a High Court stay). Section 3.3 for US$64 million cancelled, US$32 million not awarded, US$56 million not completed and the ERR discussion; section 3.4 for efficiency Substantial, outcome Moderately Unsatisfactory and 'missing 50% of the targets'. ICRR14881 section 5 and its table for efficiency Substantial, ERR 22 per cent at appraisal over 90 per cent and 47 per cent at the ICR over 97 per cent, and for 65 per cent of subprojects completed and 73 per cent disbursed.

kiidp-kampala-roads-compensation.whole: The Evaluation Group's review reports that the project expanded the Lubigi primary drainage channel, upgraded 11.81 kilometres of roads against about 14.42 kilometres planned, developed six acres of land next to the existing landfill, trained 76 staff in contract management and revenue collection, bought 25 vehicles along with information technology and records management equipment, extended the council's network to division offices, carried out its financial recovery plan, completed a strategic planning process and five public consultations, and updated the Kampala Physical Development Plan. The city council's stock of overdue liabilities fell from UGX 8 billion to zero, against an original target of UGX 3 billion and a revised target of UGX 0.5 billion, and its own-source revenue rose from UGX 22 billion in 2005/06 to UGX 55.71 billion in 2012/13, against an original target of UGX 30 billion and a revised UGX 33.5 billion, which the review attributes to the financial recovery plan and better collection of property rates, local service tax and hotel tax. Building permit approval fell from a year in 2006 to two months, and the share of property owners issued rate demand notes rose from 30 per cent in 2006 to 100 per cent in 2013. Works were dropped at the first restructuring, in December 2010, when the government's contribution fell from US$3.5 million to US$2.06 million: the secondary and tertiary drainage channel works, the area traffic management works, the landfill gas collection and flaring system, the maintenance of about 26 kilometres of tarmac roads, which government funds then paid for, and the infrastructure for the Kibuli and Kawempe markets, which other agencies planned to take up across seven Kampala markets. The review puts the economic rate of return on the road works at 29.8 per cent at completion against 32 per cent at appraisal, three of five road activities returning more than the 12 per cent discount rate and two returning less with negative net present values, which it attributes to much higher actual construction costs, and the drainage works at 17.5 per cent against 16.8 per cent at appraisal. It rates efficiency Substantial and the outcome Satisfactory, while saying that the efficiency of the US$1.6 million spent on institutional development could not be assessed, for want of information on what the council itself spent to raise its revenue and of any benchmark for an efficient revenue collection system. The public satisfaction figures used for the infrastructure objective come from Citizens Report Card surveys, which the review notes measured roads, drainage and solid waste across the whole city rather than the project's own works. The project cost US$35.64 million against US$37.1 million at appraisal, with US$33.58 million of the US$33.6 million credit disbursed and the closing date extended twice, by three years in total. Every figure here comes through the Evaluation Group's review of the completion report; all are the lender's own, and no independent check was found.
kiidp-kampala-roads-compensation.why: ICRR14588 (P078382_ICRR) is the only evaluative document for this project in the cache and was read in full; no completion report for P078382 is present, so the paragraph says the figures come through the review. Section 2c for the components with appraisal and actual costs, the two restructurings, and the list of dropped works (secondary and tertiary drainage, area traffic management, landfill gas collection and flaring, 26 km of tarmac maintenance moved to government funds, and the Kibuli and Kawempe markets with other agencies' seven-market plan) and the fall in government contribution from US$3.5m to US$2.06m. Section 2d for project cost US$35.64m against US$37.1m, US$33.58m disbursed of US$33.6m, and the two extensions totalling three years. tanzania-tscp-compensation-delays.whole: By the completion report's count the project paved or rebuilt 253.6 kilometres of non-rural road against 140 at appraisal and a target raised to 220, built or rehabilitated 42.02 kilometres of stand-alone drains against 15 and a revised 31, built or rehabilitated 277 waste collection points against 231 and a revised 255, built or improved seven sanitary landfills with 17 cells against five and a revised seven, built or improved 11 bus, daladala and lorry stands with room for 1,471 vehicles against six stands and 600 vehicles at appraisal and a revised ten and 1,100, and delivered 29 gender-sensitive features, among them paved walkways, raised humps near schools, footbridges and a playground, against a target of 17 set at restructuring. 1,890,687 people were counted as direct beneficiaries against 952,806 at appraisal and a revised 1,741,000, and 1,278,053 as having access to improved bus stations, terminals or lorry stands against 543,721 and a revised 1,266,200. Waste reaching landfills rose from 28 per cent of the waste generated to 86 per cent, against 58 per cent at appraisal and a target cut to 40 per cent because the first landfill began operating in the third quarter of 2016 rather than 2013. Own-source revenue in the eight local authorities rose 457 per cent over the 2010 base year against 45 per cent at appraisal and a revised 100 per cent, which the report attributes partly to the cities' rapid growth and to plot sales, a major revenue source, counting inside that revenue. Spending on operation and maintenance reached 28 per cent of municipal expenditure against 16 per cent at appraisal and a revised 20; fees and charges covered 84 per cent of solid waste operating costs against 12 per cent at appraisal and a revised 25, and 95 per cent of bus and lorry stand costs against 65 and a revised 80 - though the report's financial analysis says solid waste fees and charges do not cover operating costs, which it calls a risk to the facilities' sustainability. Seven local authorities had up-to-date strategic urban development plans and general planning schemes, both targets met, and all project-related grievances were recorded as addressed. Four indicators were dropped: up-to-date property valuations and property tax collected, after responsibility for valuation, billing and collection moved to the Tanzania Revenue Authority from 1 July 2016, and roads in good or fair condition and people with access to an all-season road, as measures the project did not control. Institutional strengthening work on urban planning systems, geographic information systems and own-source revenue was dropped after delays in mobilisation and the pandemic and taken up by a follow-on project, and solid waste and geographic information equipment contracts were ended by mutual agreement with suppliers who could not produce in time. The report's economic analysis of a sample of works puts the rate of return at 40 per cent with a net present value of US$65 million - 48 per cent for urban roads, 32 per cent for the Arusha landfill, 33 per cent for the Duga drainage, 13 per cent for the Tanga bus station and 12 per cent for solid waste in Tanga - against 22 per cent at appraisal over 94 per cent of project cost in the Evaluation Group's table, and says actual investment costs at appraisal prices were 10 per cent below expectations and benefits three times costs. Both the report and the review rate efficiency Substantial. All these figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.

agara-zemo-osiauri-e60-agarebi.whole: The project built 12 kilometres of two-lane dual carriageway from Agara to Zemo Osiauri, its target, maintained 67 kilometres of the E60 between Natakhtari and Ruisi under a multi-year contract, and put road safety measures and access roads on 100 kilometres of the E60 between Natakhtari and Ruisi and between Agara and Chumateleti, all recorded as delivered. Transit time from Agara to Kashuri fell from 10 minutes to 7, its target; vehicle operating costs fell from US$0.20 to US$0.18 a kilometre for cars and from US$0.76 to US$0.72 for trucks, both targets; and the road fatality rate on the Tbilisi to Senaki section of the corridor fell from 11.6 to 3.03 deaths per 100 million vehicle-kilometres against a target of 8.5 - a stretch of about 275 kilometres, which the Evaluation Group's review notes is far longer than the 12 kilometres built or the 111 kilometres given safety works, so that earlier work on policing and public awareness also bears on it. A road sector strategy taking in social and gender dimensions was adopted, as were an updated road safety strategy and action plan and a roadmap for intelligent transport systems, and the feasibility study from Zemo to Argveta and the detailed engineering design from Zemo Osiauri to Chumateleti were completed. Two rows were not delivered: the training needs assessments and manpower development plans for the Roads Department and for the ministry, replaced by a gap analysis of which one deliverable was finished under this loan and the rest moved to a follow-on project. The asset value of the East-West Highway corridor from Tbilisi to Sarpi rose by GEL 1,599 million against a target the completion report's framework gives as GEL 2,200 million and the review gives as GEL 2,300 million, about 70 per cent of it; the review attributes the gap to the delayed completion of the Samtredia to Grigoleti section financed by the European Investment Bank and to the upgrading of the Zemo Osiauri to Chumateleti Lot 2 section, whose contract was terminated in December 2018 and which was being tendered again under another project, and says this asset value is the cumulative book value of recent investments rather than a measure of economic benefit or one that accounts for depreciation. The report puts the economic rate of return at 19.9 per cent at completion against 17.5 per cent at appraisal, with a net present value at a 12 per cent discount rate that its text gives as US$37.7 million and its own table as US$37.3 million, against US$26.7 million at appraisal, and says the higher result comes mainly from reduced project costs and higher traffic than appraisal assumed, with the extension of the closing date having no effect because the civil works contract finished on time. The report rates efficiency High; the Evaluation Group's review rates it Substantial, on the road works being 56 per cent of the project as completed, a closing date two years late and some analytical work deferred. All these figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.

maluku-sez-maes-inkiene-demolition.whole: By the completion report's count 211 hectares of land at Maluku were secured by the government and developed for industrial use, with a protective wall 6,155 metres long built around them with project money; the agency for special economic zones was set up and made operational, a consultant consortium was hired to draft the regulations implementing the 2015 zone law and to update the demand study, and a private developer was selected from seven respondents with the public-private partnership signed at the end of January 2020. The report says the land was acquired under Bank policies, that a resettlement action plan was fully implemented and that some 300 land concession holders were compensated. After the mid-term review the infrastructure to be financed was cut: basic infrastructure for an initial 59 hectares was dropped, leaving the government and the developer to pay for the physical works needed, and the component's allocation fell from US$27 million at appraisal to US$6 million. Disbursement for the zone component was suspended for 14.5 months, from January 2016 to March 2017, over the borrower's non-observance of the resettlement safeguards. On the agricultural side the project rehabilitated 542 kilometres of rural road against a target of 500 and recorded 97,757 direct beneficiaries against a target of 50,000, 44 per cent of them women against a 40 per cent target. Jobs created in the selected value chains came to 5,026 against 11,000 at appraisal and a target cut to 5,000 at the 2018 restructuring, with women 19 per cent of them against a 50 per cent target. Yields were 3.1 tonnes a hectare for rice against a target of 3, 10 tonnes for palm oil against 15 at appraisal and a revised 10, and 18.4 tonnes for cassava against 20, which the report attributes partly to improved varieties already in use before the project and to growers keeping old varieties alongside new ones. Production volumes were 1,325.86 tonnes of cassava against 3,900 at appraisal and a revised 2,500, 35.4 tonnes of rice against 37 and a revised 25, and 113,656 tonnes of palm oil against 750 and a revised 450; the report's own comments on those three rows multiply every figure by a thousand and call the palm oil result 25,257 per cent of its target, so the units these volumes are reported in cannot be relied on. Processed food came to 163,861.53 tonnes against 5,000 at appraisal and a target cut to 1,000. Collection centres, including parking and warehouses, were not built, the report citing cost, difficulties over access to land and the time left to do the works. The report puts the economic rate of return at 21.9 per cent at completion against 32.4 per cent at appraisal, with a net present value of US$33.7 million, a benefit-cost ratio of 1.55 and a financial return of 21.3 per cent, and says a two-year delay in benefits would bring the rate below the 12 per cent opportunity cost of capital; it rates efficiency Substantial while the Evaluation Group's review rates it Modest. All these figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.

freetown-wellington-33kv-demolitions.whole: The project replaced and upgraded the 7.8 kilometre line from the Blackhall Road substation to Wellington by way of the Ropoti substation, from 11 kV to 33 kV on double-circuit towers, against a target of 7.5 kilometres, and rehabilitated five substations against a target of four: Wilberforce, Kingtom, Blackhall Road, Ropoti and Wellington, Ropoti being new, while Blackhall Road was only rehabilitated and its new equipment was left to be installed under another Bank project. It installed 20,000 prepaid meters, 17,800 single-phase and 2,200 three-phase, in 20 neighbourhoods of Freetown, its target, and 100 bulk meters at eight switching stations and substations against a target of 200. Losses in the project area fell from 38 per cent to 34.5 per cent against a target of 33, which the completion report calls 70 per cent of the target and describes as preliminary; the distribution utility's collection rate rose from 76 per cent to 86, its target, which the report attributes to more prepaid than postpaid customers and to a revenue protection and arrears recovery programme; and 720,000 people were counted as beneficiaries against 205,400 at appraisal and a revised 624,000, a figure derived from 120,000 households connected during implementation at six people a household. The project management unit hired six staff against seven planned and a revised four, the report adding that their technical capacity needed improvement. The rural electrification component was cancelled at the October 2015 restructuring and the third objective, increasing access to electricity in selected rural areas, was removed from the project: none of the 28 photovoltaic systems for public buildings in rural villages was installed, and that indicator was dropped at the same time. The report puts the economic rate of return at 14 per cent at completion against 39 per cent at appraisal, with a net present value of US$2.46 million over a 20-year life against US$26.7 million at appraisal, and the financial return at 33 per cent against 36 per cent with a net present value of US$23.43 million against US$11.3 million, and says the economic returns are moderate because the loss reduction investments return relatively little. Both the report and the Evaluation Group's review rate efficiency Modest. Implementation was delayed before the Ebola outbreak by the unit's limited capacity in procurement and safeguards and nearly stopped during it, with supervision missions at times moved to Abidjan, which the report says made a realistic assessment of problems on the ground impossible. All these figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.

laulara-solerema-road-structures.whole: The project rehabilitated the Dili to Ainaro corridor in five lots totalling about 109 kilometres, and by the completion report's count drainage in good condition on the corridor reached 99.96 per cent against 20 per cent at appraisal and a target raised to 90 per cent in 2017, roads in good or fair condition 99.63 per cent against 50 per cent and a revised 90, road roughness fell to 3.43 metres per kilometre from a baseline of 9 against 6.5 at appraisal and a revised 3.5, and slope protection was improved at 1,350 locations against 25 at appraisal and a revised 820, including 352 of 362 stone masonry retaining walls and all 141 gabions. Incidents needing emergency repairs on the corridor fell from 53 a year to three - a tree falling on a house in April 2022 and two fatal incidents in August and September 2022 - against 30 at appraisal and a revised 15, the unit of that indicator having changed from a percentage to a count of incidents. Traffic grew 250 per cent against a 30 per cent target, from 835 vehicles a day in 2014 to 2,926 in 2023 on the corridor count, while the report's economic analysis gives 3,048 vehicles a day in 2014 and 10,741 in 2023 at the Dili count station. Of 53 grievances recorded by 22 November 2022, four concerned environment, health and safety, 43 social matters and six resettlement, all of them on Lot 2, and all were answered within the service standard except one settled after three months. Lot 2, the Laulara to Solerema section, was taken over at 97.28 per cent of its as-built value, US$16,542,026.34, with US$462,737.61 of work outstanding on force majeure grounds and 22.21 kilometres paved, and its four-year performance-based maintenance contract was to start in June 2024; multi-year performance-based maintenance covered 79 per cent of the corridor, Lots 1, 3, 4 and 5, whose two-year contracts ended between July 2019 and February 2022. Three maintenance sub-components were cancelled when the 2013 additional financing extended the works to the whole corridor, with routine maintenance and emergency response written into the civil works contracts instead, and the emergency planning and response sub-component was cancelled at the 2017 restructuring; the procurement of two detailed engineering design packages was also cancelled. The report puts the economic rate of return at 21.4 per cent at completion with a net present value of US$59.40 million, against 18 per cent and US$2.07 million at appraisal, 14 per cent and US$13.51 million at the 2013 additional financing and 15.9 per cent and US$30.01 million at the 2017 one, and attributes the rise mainly to Lot 2's cost falling from US$26.835 million to US$18.235 million and to higher traffic. The report rates efficiency Substantial; the Evaluation Group's review rates it Modest, on an implementation period of more than ten years with seven years of extensions, project implementation support costs rising from under US$1 million at appraisal to US$3.04 million, and a reduced scope for maintenance, institutional development and community engagement. All these figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.

nigeria-federal-roads-trader-relocations.whole: The project rehabilitated 300 kilometres of federal road against a target of 442 - a figure the completion report's own key-outputs table gives as 310 - completing all 121 kilometres of the Mokwa to Bida road, 72 of 77 kilometres from Enugu to Abakaliki, 65 of 74 kilometres from Akure to Ilesha and 52 of 53 kilometres from Ogoja Junction to Ikom, while the 117 kilometre Gombe to Biu road was dropped for want of funds, the Evaluation Group's review adding that bid prices came in higher than the appraisal estimates. It upgraded or maintained 288 kilometres against 340 planned, delivering the Takai to Albasu to Gaya road in Kano in full, 10.15 of 10 kilometres from Nafada to Gombeabba and 19.4 kilometres from Ado Ilumoba to Agbado to Ikare, but only 17.5 of 48 kilometres from Hong to Mubi, 22 of 28 from Kurfi to Charanchi, 22 of 24 from Jebba to Lafiagi and 9.1 of 16.5 from Rumukurushi to Chokocho. Six pedestrian overbridges were built, the target, which the report says about 12,000 pedestrians a day use; the safe corridor approach was applied on four of five corridors, the fifth dropped for want of funds; the HDM-4 road model was calibrated for Nigeria and national road design standards were put in place, though the report notes axle load standards are not. Average travel time on the project roads fell from 120 to 60 minutes per 100 kilometres against a target of 90 cut to 80, and average vehicle operating costs from 40 to 38 US cents a vehicle-kilometre, the target. Two outcome rows fell short: the fatality rate was 143 deaths per 10,000 vehicles against a target of 120 from a baseline of 161, which the report calls an 11 per cent fall against the 25 per cent intended, and direct project beneficiaries came to 340,000 against 500,000, which the report ties to the shorter lengths of road built. The road sector database held 3,000 of the 10,000 kilometres targeted and the asset management system covered 3,000 of 6,800 kilometres. The report puts the economic rate of return on the rehabilitated roads at 58.08 per cent at completion against 53 per cent at appraisal, with the present value of net benefits at US$821.81 million against US$169 million, and on the roads given upgrading or periodic maintenance at 47.59 per cent against 46 per cent, with net benefits of US$251.19 million against US$146 million, covering 77 per cent of total project cost; it rates efficiency Substantial. The Evaluation Group's review rates efficiency Modest, on long delays, significant cost increases and the downsizing of the project's scope, and notes the project closed six months late. All these figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.

addo-park-farm-worker-rehousing.whole: By the completion report's count the protected terrestrial area around the park grew from 141,000 hectares to 170,115, against 236,000 planned at appraisal and a target cut to 205,000 in September 2007, which the report calls 83 per cent achieved. Of the marine area, 7,414 hectares were declared, Bird Island and St Croix, with the 120,000 hectares of the planned marine protected area submitted and awaiting final approval at closing. Private land brought into the park through conservation partnerships came to 17,608 hectares against 46,000 at appraisal and a target cut to 30,000, with a further 11,000 hectares of community land awaiting incorporation by the Enon Bersheba communities trust, the report saying land titling questions proved more complicated than expected. Wildlife was fenced within 133,000 hectares against a target of 130,000, alien species were cleared from 75,044 hectares against 65,000, a monitoring and management information system was built whose environmental component was later used in 22 other parks, 11 small enterprises with more than three permanent employees and two years of trading were created against a target of 10, three partnership agreements were signed and six commercial concessions were operating, all targets, and an environmental education centre was built that the report says about 12,806 primary and secondary school students visit a year. Employment in the greater park area rose from 1,228 people to 1,842 against a target of 1,596, 514 training days a year were delivered against 350, and 32 learnerships and internships against 30. Tourist entries rose from 94,699 in 2004 to 135,109 in 2010, against 180,000 at appraisal and a revised target of 120,000, and tourist accommodation went from 174 beds to 505. The park's revenue covered 132 per cent of the cost of managing it in 2009/10, against 94.6 per cent at the project's start, making it one of the few parks in South Africa whose revenue exceeds its operating costs, and the government's counterpart funding rose from US$28 million to US$54 million. No economic or financial rate of return was calculated at appraisal or at completion, the report saying such calculations were not required for a stand-alone grant of this kind and would be very hard to produce after the event. Both the completion report and the Evaluation Group's review rate efficiency Substantial, and the review rates the outcome Moderately Satisfactory against the report's Satisfactory, on the ground that the data do not show how far poverty was reduced: there are no figures in the report on changes in tourism revenues or on how many people moved out of marginal traditional farming into better paid tourism work. All these figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.
